transcript.content: Hello, welcome in. I'm Dr. Smith. To start, can you tell me what's been bringing you in to see me today?

Hi Dr. Smith. I guess what brings me in is... well, I got pretty worked up in a staff meeting at work recently. I started acting out this whole fall-prevention drill right there in the room. I was moving chairs around, waving my arms all over the place to show them how to do it... and I just couldn't seem to stop. Even when folks were telling me to sit down and relax, I just kept going. So, that's mostly why I'm here today.
How long has this period of unusually high energy and activity been going on?

Well, it's... it hasn't just been this one time. These stretches of being way too energized, where I'm sleeping very little and pushing all these big plans... they've been coming and going for about 11 months now.
During these periods of high energy and racing activity, have you been using any alcohol, drugs, or other substances?
No, I haven't been taking anything like that. I don't drink or use any drugs, and I'm not taking any medications either. It's just... this energy just happens on its own, I guess.

During these periods of high energy, have you ever heard voices, seen things others don't see, or had beliefs that others found unusual or untrue—like feeling you had special powers or were being watched?

Yeah, um... I have. When I was in those really fired-up stretches, you know, sleeping just a few hours and making all those big plans... I was also hearing things. Like, I'd hear calls for me that just weren't there. And... well, I was also feeling absolutely sure that my supervisor was setting traps for me at work. I just really believed it at the time.

Have you ever experienced these voices or the belief that your supervisor was plotting against you at times when you were NOT in one of these high-energy, low-sleep periods—that is, when your mood and energy felt normal?

Yeah, I have. Um... there was a calmer stretch where I was actually sleeping more normally, and I wasn't rushing around with all those projects. I felt pretty regular. But even then, for several weeks, I still heard my name being called out. And I stayed completely convinced that people at work were keeping notes on me. So, yeah, it happened even when my energy was fine.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient reports recurrent manic episodes (elevated energy, decreased need for sleep, increased goal-directed activity, pressured/uncontrollable behavior) occurring intermittently over 11 months, with concurrent psychotic symptoms (auditory hallucinations of hearing his name called, paranoid delusions that his supervisor was plotting against him). Critically, he also endorses these same psychotic symptoms (hallucinations and paranoid delusions) persisting for several weeks during a period when his mood and energy were normal (euthymic), independent of any mood episode. Substance use and general medical causes were ruled out. This pattern—mood episode plus psychotic symptoms, with psychotic symptoms also present for a significant duration (≥2 weeks) in the absence of a prominent mood episode, and mood symptoms present for a substantial portion of the illness—meets criteria for Schizoaffective Disorder, Bipolar Type (F25.0), rather than Bipolar I Disorder with psychotic features (which requires psychosis only during mood episodes) or Schizophrenia (which would require mood symptoms to be brief relative to total illness duration).
